name: Hiram
overview: Hiram was a male king of Tyre, known primarily from the biblical account in 2 Samuel 5:11. He is recognized for his political role rather than tribal affiliation, as Scripture does not specify his tribe. His reign as king is significant in the context of Israel's history during the time of King David.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Hiram' means '[my] brother is elevated,' reflecting a Hebrew meaning associated with elevation or honor. He is also known by the variant name 'Huram,' which carries the same meaning. His title 'King of Tyre' identifies his royal position over the city of Tyre, an important Phoenician city-state.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Hiram beyond his designation as King of Tyre. There are no additional familial connections or relationships noted in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Hiram's significance lies in his role as an ally to King David, providing support to Israel during David's reign. His kingship over Tyre placed him in a position to assist in the building projects and political consolidation of Israel. This cooperation reflects God's providence in securing alliances that furthered the establishment of David's kingdom.
